data.narrative:
Base Power, a Series C climate and energy company founded by Zach Dell and Justin Lopas, is evaluated against a frontier-tech comp universe of 9 private and 1 public peer (LNZA). The three most directly comparable same-sector, same-stage peers—KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M)—establish a valuation range floor and ceiling.

Two valuation methods triangulate to a defensible range. The stage-progression method applies a typical 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier to the $1.0B total raised proxy, implying $1.7B. The peer-median method across the three direct comparables yields $1.0B, with a wide interquartile spread ($700M–$3.0B) reflecting market heterogeneity within frontier energy. Cross-sector peers including Helion and Redwood Materials provide secondary reference points but are weighted secondarily due to operational divergence.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $850M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.4B. This range reflects tension between the normalized peer median ($1.0B) and the stage-appropriate step-up ($1.7B). Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to peers, technology validation progress, and the wide dispersion in contemporaneous Series C frontier-energy valuations, which limits precision in any point estimate.
